properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/30/2025 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: K PETROLEUM INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/30/2025
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8254340
Permit API: 125-22515
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/30/2025
Comments: On October 30th, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Mclvaine well site located in Somerset Township, Washington County following a voicemail and phone conversation where Operator Robert Inghram notified the Department of a 7-10 gallon release of crude oil from the production tank on to the ground within the tanks earthen dike. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead and a well posting fixed to the meter box on site, both of which had all required information posted on it. No active surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead, meter box, separator or fenced in production equipment on site.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed a black tank to be within an earthen dike. The tank was observed to have orange/tan smudges and dried drip marks going down the side of it. What the Department believes may be peatsorb was observed on the ground at the base of the tank on top of puddles of fluid. This fluid had a possibly petroleum based odor and was observed to have an orange/tan film on top of it in some areas.The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the dike and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.826 mS and 0.904 mS in the release area, and 0.582 mS in berm of the dike. The Department also collected soil conductivity readings of 0.1705 mS and 0.1746 mS outside of where the peatsorb was observed. All of these readings were then compared to a background soil conductvitiy reading of 0.242 mS. The readings collected outside of the peatsorb are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the release may be contained to the areas where peatsorb is observed. The readings within the fluid and in the side of the berm are elevated when compared to the background reading subjugating that the release has yet to be fully cleaned up.The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills. The Operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.While on site, the Department spoke with Operator Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's findings and of the aforementioned recommendations and requests. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for a 7-10 gallon release on to the ground from the production tank.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/17/2026 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/17/2026
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8271242
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2026
Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. Water was not observed to be actively discharging out of this culvert outlet as it appears the inlet may be blocked and resulting in seepage of water along other portions of the access road downslope. The DEP notes that no E and S controls appeared to be installed anywhere along the shared access road. Violations are being issued at this time for sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) and for failure to install E and S controls during earth disturbance activity.At the time of this inspection, no other active E and S issues were observed along the shared portions of Wildcat Road, however, the shared road was not stabilized with gravel and is exhibiting the potential for other E and S issues to occur.The DEP recommends the Operator remove the sediment from the WOC, stabilize the access road, unblock/replace the culvert pipe and install E and S controls along the access road to prevent any further e and s issues.Upon inspection of the direct portion of the access road, conditions appear to be unchanged, the DEP observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised.At the time of this inspection, the gas well site was still observed to be overgrown with vegetation. A well tag with all required information posted on it was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the gas wellhead or other production equipment on site at this time, however, a strong gas odor and hissing sound was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. OGI assistance is being requested at this time to assess the gas wellhead for a gas release. Refer to IR 4183514 for the continuation of violations for heavily rusted production equipment.While onsite, the DEP called the number on the well tag in an attempt to notify the operator of the new violations, however, the number was not in service. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road are being continued, and new violations are being issued for sediment entering WOC and failure to implement E and S controls.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/15/2024 to EQT CHAP LLC in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2024
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8188099
Permit API: 129-28483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2024
Comments: On May 15, 2024 the Department conducted a follow up inspection of EQTs Cook Unit 17H well pad in response to IR 3747032 where violations were issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs. At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road which appeared stabilized and the ERP was present in the on-site mailbox. There are two wells on this pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H has it's well tag present with all necessary information posted, and no fluid discharges or fluid leaks were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers and was not in secondary containment however, well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 proclamation of chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. The production tank appeared to be equipped for production with no observable fluid leaks or fluid discharge coming from it. The Department is again recommend the Operator continue to monitor the secondary containment to ensure that fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout, as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site (where violations were initially issued for during IR 3747032) still appears to be in violation. It is apparent that some riprap was added to the outlet and that some seeding/mulching was done by the appearance of vegetation looking fuller behind the riprap outlet, but pooling of fluid and saturated grass can be seen directly behind the riprap outlet and follows the channel that was once leading to the agricultural field behind the well site. While on site, the department contacted Jeremy Barber a representative of EQT to let them know that the riprap apron is still failing to prevent channelize flow from occurring. Jeremy stated that they will be sending an NOV response on May 16, 2024 notating that some maintenance was done and that they plan to continue to monitor it. Jeremy also stated that EQT would beef up the riprap apron some more to hopefully prevent this channelize flow from continuing to occur, and is going to think of a way to further prevent this without effecting all the grass surrounding the well site. Jeremy will set up a walk through of the well site with the Department after more maintenance is done on the riprap outlet.Based on todays inspection, violations issued under IR 3747032 will remain outstanding for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.

SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/08/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8233424
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2025
Comments: On 5/8/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 50 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. I was unaccompanied when inspecting the north pad. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead, the sand separators all connected to one gas-buster style frac tank. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up on the first well, the 206HU, and had started drilling on 4/30/2025. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. Nine frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness a 30' x 2.5' x4" deep liquid puddle east of center pad outfall that field tested at 5.58 mS conductance. A white substance was observed in the bottom of the liquid. I collected sample 9551178 from this puddle. Liquid flowing from the center pad outfall and into the sediment basin field tested at 4.82 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-179 from this area. I collected sample 9551-180 from soil in the bottom of the basin near the north-central pad outlet; the soil field tested at 2.414 mS conductance. Water in the sediment basin field tested at 2.10 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551181 near the east sediment basin overflow weir.Water flowing past the compost filter sock below the sediment basin field tested at 1.717 mS conductance. This water flows past the site LOD. I collected sample 9551182 from this area.After the inspection, I discussed the elevated conductance and sample collection with Seneca's Carlos Martinez.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1215 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/22/2025 to MINARD RUN OIL CO in Jenks Township, Forest county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MINARD RUN OIL CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8259793
Permit API: 053-26767
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone call made by Dan McCamey, of Minard Run Oil Company (MROC) on December 22, 2025. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred at Warrant 5107 Well #25P (API# 053-26767). A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

A failure in the buried steel pipeline leading to this well resulted in leaking crude oil rising to the surface. A well tender spotted the crude oil earlier today and notified MROC immediately. A work crew arrived soon thereafter to repair the line, install containment, and begin remediating the released crude oil. Upon my arrival to the site, the pipeline had been repaired which stopped the release. The released crude oil had migrated down the road ditch for approximately 20 feet, across the road through a culvert, flowing downhill into a spring, ultimately entering Guiton Run (HQ-CWF) at (41.513992, -79.18582) after traveling approximately 50 yards. Pockets of weathered crude oil and emulsion were evident downstream for approximately 475 yards ending at (41.512156, -79.189991). The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident was unknown due to the lack of accumulated product at the site. At this time, it is estimated that less than one barrel of product was released. A siphon dam was installed in the road ditch, beyond the direction of flow where the crude oil was initially spotted. A second siphon dam was installed and lined beyond the road culvert. Booms and diapers were already placed on the surface and at the point of entry in Guiton Run. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. Additional booms and diapers should be placed in Guiton Run to absorb and capture any released crude oil within the stream. The stream should be continuously monitored until there is no longer any evidence of crude oil. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor remediation of this release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will need to be conducted to verfiy that the cleanup is deemed complete prior to any seeding/mulching. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The conventional well was equipped for production with a pump jack. The well name, API number, and operator information were displayed on a sign attached to the pump jack.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/31/2025
Comments: On January 31, 2025 the Department conducted an Incident inspection of the PF Eisaman South 43 well pad located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on Monday, January 27, 2025. Accompanying on today's inspection is CNX representative Jessie Valentine. Mr. Valentine showed the Department the area where the spill occurred and stated that the spill occurred due to a piping/equipment failure, and that the release was approximately two barrels of production fluid.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Valentine stated that remediation efforts had occurred, and that fresh gravel has been laid in the spill area. The Department observed a large area between the production tanks and GPUs where new gravel appeared to be laid. The Department took a background soil conductivity reading upslope on the well pad's perimeter (0.0894 mS), and then took several readings in the area where fresh gravel was laid (0.0103 mS, 0.492 mS, 0.0436 mS, 9.68 mS, 6.38 mS, 0.787 mS, and 0.413 mS) to assess if any impacted materials remained on site. These soil conductivity readings when compared to the background soil conductivity reading subjugate that there are still some areas where the spill has not been fully excavated. Mr. Valentine spray painted the areas where the Department took elevated readings at, so they can easily identified for future remediation. The Department recommends the Operator fully remediate the release and dispose of all contaminated material properly and in accordance with regulations. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, plan for further remediation of the spill or release and assessment of any impacts to water of the Commonwealth. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled and is requesting the Operator follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2). At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and inside the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) Plan. The Ac 9 sign had a different Operator than the ERP and PPC Plan, the Department recommends the Operator update all plans as applicable. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed, and all of the well pad perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the well pad had 6 wells on it on it as well as 3 production tanks within secondary containment and 6 GPUs within secondary containment, at the time of this inspection no active fluid leaks or fluid discharge were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. The 2H well (SPUD 4/20/2017) had a well tag fixed to it with the API number on it, but this well tag did not have any of the Operator's information on it. The Department is recommending the Operator update the well tag and/or well posting to have all required information posted on it in accordance with 3211(g). While on site, the Department spoke with CNX representative Chad Eisenman via the phone to inform him of the Department's findings during this inspection and verbally requested the aforementioned information.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for an approximately 2 barrel release of production fluid onto the well pad. A subsequent inspection will be conducted to assess further remedial measures. An Act 2 Report has not yet been submitted to the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: William H Brawand
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-10-04

Violation ID: 864251
Permit API: 047-24421
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-04
Comments: This inspection was performed following the Department receiving a complaint of possible brine dumping in a ditch line near the Brawand 53 well location. This inspection was performed with WQSS Rich Sheriff. The well is equipped with an electric powered pumpjack, and appears to be producing. The stuffing box seems to have leaked at times, as there is a coating of oil on the wellhead and ground. The well is tagged and the access road and site are stable. There is a ditch line/UNT to Johnson Run that flows near the entrance to this site. The ditch flows to the southeast and into a small pond approximately 500 feet away, which has an outlet to continue down-gradient. A check with a handheld conductivity meter and probe shows elevated levels in this channel immediately around a culvert and at various spots flowing downstream. There is also evidence of tree and other vegetative death along the immediate banks of this UNT, indicating that brine was likely discharged into this channel. (See attached photos) The Operator may contact WQSS Rich Sheriff at 814-723-0973 to discuss this incident.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/13/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/13/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 978491
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/13/2022
Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-23 to Seneca Resources Co Llc in Sergeant Twp, McKean county. 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-23
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 887191
Permit API: 083-57162
Unconventional: Yes
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-23
Comments: At 17:48 on Saturday (6/20/20), Doug Kepler reported a hose rupture on well pad D08-O that resulted in the discharge of 110-120 barrels of production fluid to containment. Doug Kepler reported about 8-10 barrels of fluid overflowed containment onto a gravel road. It was determined that the spill flowed for 3-4 minutes prior to being noted and then shut off. At the time of this inspection, the operator was in the process of removing the contaminated soil from the impacted area. The containment was vacuumed dry and then removed. A mini excavator and rolloff containers were brought on site. Screening was done of the impacted soil using a soil conductivity meter with a probe. It was determined that the production water flowed along the access road approximately 200-250 feet in a narrow band before exiting the road surface in a small depression. The operator had removed all the impacted soil in this stretch at the time of this inspection. They were loading their 11th container at this time. An excavation was developing deeper on the northeast side of the spill site, where elevated conductivity was noted several feet into the soil. The operator will continue to screen and remove soil today and for as long as necessary. Rolloff containers are being staged on the D08-O pad, which is just off the edge of the spill location. Further follow up of this spill location will be performed as necessary.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2025
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8231845
Permit API: 033-25027
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/02/2025
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-25207 on May 02, 2025. Earth disturbance actives were observed around the production equipment. No E and S issues were observed. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected.Please note during the inspection I observed a small drip coming from the release valve on the brine tank. I screened for conductivity all around the edge of the brine tank, readings ranged from 1.46 mS/cm to > 4.00 mS /cm. Please note, the Hanna soil probes max range is 4.00 mS/cm. Elevated readings range ~1-2ft. away from the brine tank. While onsite I notified Will Warfel and Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC. According to the lease operator, the fluids were last measured on April 2, 2025. The lease operator remeasured the fluids after I reported the leak. The measurement is ~1/2 inch lower than last month's fluids level within the tank. Therefore, they estimated ~10-15 gallons of fluids were released. The leak on the release valve was later fixed by the lease operator. Clean-up will take place during the week of May 5, 2025.Violations have been cited for the brine release.

Report Details

Comments: On August 22, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022.Precision Drilling Rig 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the 1003H lateral. Precision Drilling has already drilled the 1005H well and have one more well lateral to complete. There were 8 oil based mud tanks, 4 cement tanks, 5 frac tanks and 4 floc water tanks in secondary containment. The containment around the drill rig was in good condition. A vacuum truck is onsite to vacuum up the water in the secondary containment. STL Resources was in the process of pumping out the northwest stormwater vault on the well pad from recent rainfall. The water from the northwest stormwater vault was being pumped into 5 frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter. The water in the southwest stormwater vault was about 6 feet from the top of the vault. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 2 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 33.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 76.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Three monitoring wells have been drilled about 50 yards to the west of the well pad. All the infiltration berms at the site have been hydro seeded. The percent vegetated cover varies from berm to berm. The recently rebuilt northwest and southwest infiltration berms at the well pad are beginning to become vegetated. The water in the northwest infiltration berm was screened for conductivity and resulted in 230 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/20/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8271756
Permit API: 047-24975
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Alexis Jacobs, WQS with the Department, on April 20th, 2026. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on the E08-T well pad.It was reported that approximately 1 barrel of production fluid was released from a maintenance failure on a pump used to support the transport of production fluid through a pipeline. The failure was immediately addressed and corrected to stop the production fluid from leaving the pipeline. The pump was in secondary containment, although a majority of the production fluid discharged outside of the containment onto the well pad and onto the fill material beyond the well pad. Upon arrival to the site, a skid steer was being used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. One dumpster was on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. A second dumpster was being transported to the site at the time of this inspection. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred on the well pad. A mini excavator was used to scrape approximately an inch of surface material from the pad where the spill occurred. This material was in a pile to be removed from the pad and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The impacted soils beyond the edge of the well pad were also excavated and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The excavated area beyond the pad was approximately 10 yards x 5 yards. Evidence of production fluid did not appear to be present beyond the excavated area. A copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department when available.Confirmatory field sampling will need to occur to confirm full remediation of the site. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) completed an administrative inspection on Seneca Resource's Peffer Strong 483 35H on 10/5/2022. The inspection was conducted to summarize analytical sample results from samples collected on 9/6/2022 at the well site.On 7/7/2022, violations of 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301 were cited against API #117-22110 based on analytical sample results from a sample collected on 6/23/2022 indicating the presence of a regulated substance on the pad surface, off containment. Three areas with the presence of material or water with elevated conductivity were identified in the 6/23/2022 inspection report: pooled fluid near the entrance of the pad, pad material in front of the produced water offload area and pad material located just southeast of the gas processing unit's (GPUs) containment.On 9/6/2022, the pad surface area located just southeast of the GPUs' secondary containment was retaining fluid that was field measured at ~3.72mS/cm. Sample 0983-344 was collected from the pooled fluid. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #2). Just east of the GPUs' containment structure, a rock-lined channel used for the conveyance of stormwater into the site's sediment traps is located at the base of the pad's cut slope. On 9/6/2022, fluid within the channel was field measured at ~2.30mS/cm and sample 0983-343 was collected for the channel. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #3).On 9/6/2022, the secondary containment structure surrounding the wellheads and processing equipment near the center of the pad was observed to be actively overflowing. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e) regarding the failure to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more was cited against API #117-22110. Seneca Resource's notice of violation response is attached as a file and will be uploaded to eFACTS. Sample 0983-345 was collected from fluid with a sheen observed overtopping the containment structure. The analytical sample results for this sample are attached as a file and photo (photo #1).The DEP highly recommends conducting additional screening and potential remedial work.Violations of the following cited against API #117-22110 will remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e)

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/01/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 987208
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/01/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple releases on Pad B for which violations remain outstanding. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B on permit 081-21880.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid from the MASS from 12/19/22.
